sentences.text: For Appellant : Mr.C.Prasanna  For R1 : Mr.Leonard Ar  Government Ad  For R2 & R3 : Mr.A.Arasu Ga  JUDGMENT This Criminal Appeal is filed by the appellant/defacto complainant/PW1 to set aside the judgment of acquittal rendered in S.C.No.132 of 2014 dated 12.10.2015 acquitting the respondents 2 and 3 by the learned Sessions Judge, Mahila Court, Cuddalore.
2.The case of the prosecution is that the marriage between the deceased Rajalakshmi and the second respondent/Suresh was held on 31.05.2012 and it was an arranged marriage.
The third respondent is the mother of the second respondent.
At the time of the marriage, 15 sovereigns of jewels, a wooden bureau, a cot, household articles, brass and silver utensils and a Honda motorcycle were given as sridhana.
After the marriage, the demand for dowry continued.
The victim/Rajalakshmi was harassed.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
During tradition re-aligning of mangalsutra, three sovereigns of gold chain was demanded.

Further the third respondent claimed that the second respondent was in demand, that there were offers for 50 sovereigns of jewels and a car for the and hence, there was constant dowry demand despite a separate independent house being set up for the second respondent and Rajalakshmi by the parents of Rajalakshmi.
Even for Aadi festival, the traditional visit of married girl to her parents' house along with her husband not taken place and the victim Rajalakshmi was continuously harassed.
The victim was subjected to cruelty which peaked to the extent that the said Rajlakshmi could not bear anymore and on 26.09.2012 within seven months of marriage, committed suicide by hanging.

On getting information, the appellant/defacto complainant/father of the victim lodged a complaint to the first respondent and initially a case under Section 174 Cr.P.C. in Crime No.397 of 2012 registered.

Thereafter, the respondent police visited the scene of occurrence, prepared observation mahazar and rough sketch in the presence of the witnesses and the articles found in the scene of occurrence seized.

Since the death was taken place within seven years of marriage, FIR and case records submitted to P.W.13/Revenue Divisional Officer who https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
Uploaded on: 22/10/2025 07:18:58 pm ) conducted inquest on 26.09.2012 at about 5.00 p.m.

During the inquest, he examined the neighbors of the deceased, her parents, her brother and family members of the deceased, her father-in-law, her mother-in-law and husband of the deceased and filed a report on 20.11.2012 confirming that the respondents 2 and 3 were not happy with the Ramamurthy vs The Superintendent Of Police on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168637974/
2 sridhana articles presented and there was constant dowry demand on all occasions.

sentences.text: Lastly, a washing machine was demanded as Deepavali sridhana for which the parents of the deceased Rajalakshmi informed that they would make arrangements but sought some time.
The neighbors informed that they had never seen the deceased and the second respondent in a happy mood.
Further, it was found that one Latha, neighbour was contacted by the second respondent who advised her to lock the bureau and also keep the jewels safely.

Not concerned about the death of his wife, the second respondent seems to be more particular of jewels and wealth and on the statement of the family members and others, the RDO in his report/Ex.P7 confirmed that it is a case of dowry death and needs further investigation.

Thereafter, P.W.15 took up investigation, examined the witnesses, recorded their statements and after collecting the postmortem report and other materials, filed charge sheet in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 22/10/2025 07:18:58 pm ) this case against respondents 2 and 3.

During the trial, P.W.1 to P.W.15 examined,
Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 marked, MO1 and MO2 produced on the side of the prosecution.
On the side of defence, no witness examined and Ex.D1 marked.

The Trial Court on conclusion of trial found that the prosecution failed to prove the case beyond all reasonable doubt and acquitted both the accused/respondents 2 and 3.
3.The
contention of the learned counsel for the appellant/defacto complainant is that he had four children, two sons and two daughters, the victim/Rajalakshmi is one of his daughter.
The marriage between the second respondent and Rajalakshmi was fixed through a broker and during the marriage, he presented 17 sovereigns of gold jewels, household articles including motorbike.
The marriage was held on 31.05.2012.

The appellant presented all these sridhana articles with the fond hope that his daughter will have a happy married life and the second respondent being a School Teacher, he would be soft, cultured and take care of his daughter.

After the marriage, he had also made arrangements for a separate house for the second respondent and his daughter at Seval Street,
Neyveli and as per the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 22/10/2025 07:18:58 pm )
tradition and custom, he purchased all the provisions and set up the independent house, after the marriage, the third respondent immediately wanted to verify the genuineness of jewels and its weight which hurt his daughter very badly and later the daughter found that the respondents 2 and 3 were more on materials than on the person and they were claiming that if the marriage was with somebody else, the second respondent would have been gifted with more sridhana articles and jewels.
She was constantly harassed.

The daughter had not informed the defacto complainant initially about the incident and later when she was refused to visit during the month of Aadi, then only he came to know that the demand and harassment.

In this case, P.W.1 to P.W.4 are the father,
mother and two brothers of the deceased/Rajalakshmi, P.W.5 is a relative, P.W.6 is a known person to both the families, P.W.7 to P.W.9 are the neighbors, P.W.10 is a nearby resident, P.W.11, a relative of Rajalakshmi and witness for the observation mahazar, P.W.12 is the Doctor who conducted postmortem, P.W.13 is the RDO who conducted inquest, P.W.14 is the Sub-Inspector of Police who registered FIR and P.W.15 is the Investigating Officer in this case.

All the witnesses deposed supporting the case of the prosecution and Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (

The Trial Court for small contradictions gave the benefit of doubt and acquitted both the accused.
Hence, the above appeal filed.

sentences.text:
At the time of marriage, the defacto complainant presented 17 sovereigns of gold jewels,
household articles and a motorcycle as Sridhana.
But thereafter, the victim Rajalakshmi was constantly harassed by her husband and mother-in-law by demanding dowry.
Unable to bear the demand of dowry and harassment at the hands of the respondents 2 and 3, the said Rajalakshmi committed suicide by hanging.
On receipt of the complaint/Ex.P1, P.W.14/Sub-Inspector of Police registered FIR/Ex.P8.
Initially, a case was registered under Section 174 Cr.P.C. and since the death was occurred within seven years of marriage, FIR and case records sent to P.W.13/RDO for conducting inquest.
P.W.13/RDO conducted inquest and submitted his report/Ex.P7.

Thereafter,
P.W.15/Investigating https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 22/10/2025 07:18:58 pm )
Officer took up investigation, altered the sections vide Alteration report/Ex.P10, visited the scene of occurrence, prepared observation mahazar/Ex.P2, rough sketch/Ex.P9, examined the witness and recorded their statements, seized the articles found in the scene of occurrence under seizure mahazar/Ex.P3 and sent the body for postmortem.
The Postmortem Doctor conducted postmortem and issued a Postmortem report/Ex.P6.

After collecting the postmortem report and other materials,
charge sheet filed in this case.
5.The learned counsel appearing for the respondent 2 and 3 submitted that third respondent/mother of the first respondent is no more.
The second respondent is a Teacher.
The marriage between the second respondent and the deceased Rajalakshmi was held on 31.05.2012 and they were living happily as husband and wife as a nucleus family.
Both of them were preparing for TNPSC Group-I exam and were preparing together.
They used to sit together and study till late night.
Likewise, on the day prior to the occurrence till 2.00 a.m., they were studying together and thereafter, they went to sleep.

On the next day i.e., on 26.09.2012 when he got up, his wife https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 22/10/2025 07:18:58 pm ) was still sleeping and when he inquired, she informed that she was not feeling well and could not cook for him.
The second respondent went to the School as usual and for lunch, when he came back home, he found the door locked inside and there was no response.
He further submitted that during the marriage on 31.05.2012 articles presented to the bride and bridegroom as sridhana and not on any demand.
After the marriage, they were living independently.
The second respondent was employed as a School Teacher in Tagore Matric Higher Secondary School and was having a decent earning.
During the month of Aadi, when the parents of his wife had come to call her, she informed the respondent met with an accident, taking treatment and was in need of her help and she cannot come home.
Further, Rajlakshmi became pregnant and she underwent abortion not once but twice hence she was psychologically down.
In fact, her brother Gnanasekaran/P.W.3 took her for a day to his house for change of place.
These facts not informed to the respondent police as well as to the RDO.
The second respondent informed all these facts giving details about the Hospital where he took his wife for treatment.
His wife after two abortions in a short span of period was psychologically down, might be the reason for her to have taken https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 22/10/2025 07:18:58 pm ) extreme step and committed suicide.
But due to the sudden death of his daughter, in a shock of mind, not enquiring the real reason, the defacto complainant/appellant lodged the complaint.

The Trial Court considering the facts and materials found the complaint was with Ramamurthy vs The Superintendent Of Police on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168637974/
4 exaggeration.

sentences.text: There were contradiction in the evidence of family memebrs of the deceased and found there was no demand of dowry and the second respondent not abetted the suicide of the victim.
In fact, the parents and family members of his wife projected as though the second respondent assaulted his wife, committed murder and thereafter hung her in the nylon rope to project as suicide.
The Doctor and the postmortem report clearly confirm that it is a case of suicide.
Ligature marks were found and the final opinion confirmed victim Rajalakshmi died of asphyxia due to hanging.
The second respondent produced the Doctor's prescription dated 12.07.2012 for the treatment taken at Anjali Hospital for pregnancy and abortion.

Considering all these facts, the Trial Court acquitted the respondents 2 and 3.
6.The

learned counsel for the respondents 2 and 3 submitted that the appellant made unwanted allegation due to sudden shock and untimely https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
22/10/2025 07:18:58 pm ) death of his daughter on 26.09.2012.
During investigation, household articles, jewels of Rajalakshmi were collected and taken by her family members.
In fact 5 sovereigns of gold jewels and left over articles which were with the second respondent was collected from him on 23.03.2017 and handed over to P.W.3/Gnanasekaran.
P.W.3 had given a confirmation letter that he received the sridhana articles from him.

7.Now the issue got resolved and a joint compromise memo filed by the appellant and the second respondent.

A scanned reproduction of the same is as follows:
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 22/10/2025 07:18:58 pm )
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 22/10/2025 07:18:58 pm )
8.From the joint compromise, it is seen that now all the articles have been handed over.

Added to it,
the second respondent paid a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- to the defacto complainant for the marriage expenses and in lieu of some missing jewels.

The defacto complainant was present, he confirms receipt of the articles and also his complaint was a knee-jerk reaction impulsive due to the loss of his daughter, after passage of time, he came to know that his daughter committed suicide due to two abortions in a short span of period and she was in a depressed mood psychologically affected.

He confirmed that the second respondent broke open the door and attempted to save her and he was the person who brought her down, he went to the Police Station informed the suicide of his wife and participated in the RDO enquiry and he is not the reason for his daughter's suicide and not abetted her in any manner.
Thus the defacto complainant ascertained with neighbours, friends and relatives.
Hence he is not interested to proceed with the appeal and seeks permission to withdraw the appeal.
In view of the above, this Court finds that the judgments of the Trial Court needs no inference.
The acquittal and discharge of the respondents 2 and 3 is hereby confirmed.
